Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Australia's first innings! The umpires and the players of Pakistan are out in the middle with Nathan Lyon padded up in the dressing room. It will be the regular opening pair of Usman Khawaja and David Warner to come out and face the music. Warner gets a resounding welcome as this could well be his final Test knock and a lovely gesture from the Pakistan team as they give him a guard of honour. We might get just an over or two at best and it will be the off-spinner Sajid Khan to bowl to David Warner first up. Four fielders in and around the bat, let's go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Australia will be thoroughly disappointed with how things ended but will have to shrug it off when they come out to bat in a few minutes' time. They started off brilliantly with ball in hand as all three frontline pacers got into the wickets but every now and then, they let things slip. But when the ball got older and the pitch lost the little bite it had to begin with, the bowlers struggled. Skipper Pat Cummins though bowled really well and picked up a third five-wicket haul in a row. Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and particularly Nathan Lyon were unimpressive after Tea but Lyon did finish things up. The onus is now on the opening pair of Australia to see them through to Day 2. Stick around as Australia's reply is up next.

Pakistan went into Tea being 198/6 and with Sajid Khan and Agha Salman at the crease and they added a few vital runs before Khan got out and then Salman too fell just as he brought up his fifty. All of a sudden they were 9 down but Jamal managed things pretty well and played some eye-catching shots as well. What looked like a stellar cameo ended up being a knock to remember as he took the Aussie bowlers apart one by one and a big mention has to go to Mir Hamza as well who hung on and gave Jamal the opportunity to express himself. The Pakistani bowlers will surely be fired up after that.

Take a bow, Aamer Jamal and he has changed the entire game with that unreal 82-run knock. Right then, Australia have eventually been able to bowl out Pakistan for 313 runs and that is surely way more than they would have wished for 47/4 and then 227/9 as well. Given the nature of the pitch, it is still a slightly under-par score but Aamer Jamal has really given his side something to bowl at.

OUT! CAUGHT! Finally, finally Aamer Jamal finds the fielder and Nathan Lyon does get his man. This is tossed up on the stumps yet again and Jamal does skip down the track and go after it. Jamal heaves it away but doesn't quite get the timing and finds Mitchell Starc at long on who makes no mistake. A phenomenal inning though from the number 9 and Pakistan have been bundled out for a decent total of 313 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the final session on Day 1! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the Australian players on what is quite a muggy afternoon at the SCG. Sajid Khan and Agha Salman are all set to resume their stay on the crease. Skipper, Pat Cummins with his tail up is raring to get proceedings underway with the ball after the break.
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Pakistan have crept back slightly into the game and will look to pile up as many runs as possible. Whereas, Australia will look to get them out quickly and get more than a few overs of batting themselves in the final session. A riveting final session of play awaits. Stay tuned.

Australia, on the other hand, started right on the money with the introduction of Mitchell Marsh, who created an opportunity and got a wicket off his first over, but the No Ball disrupted his celebrations. But soon enough he did dismiss Shan Masood and broke the partnership. Nathan Lyon was taken to the cleaners by Rizwan and Salman and the Aussies leaked runs in the middle of the session. But it was Pat Cummins, the man with the golden arm yet another time who provided another crucial breakthrough as he dismissed Mohammed Rizwan and picked his third wicket. Australia dropped a couple of catches and were sloppy going by their standards. But they would be happy to have seen the back of Rizwan.

This brings us to the end of the Second Session of Day 1 as the players head for Tea. Pakistan began cautiously negotiating with the lethal pace battery of the hosts. Of what looked like a pretty good surface to bat on, Pakistani batters were tentative in their approach. Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood weaved a good partnership for the fifth wicket for 49 runs. But Masood perished sooner after surviving on a No Ball and Pakistan were taken aback with the long tail to follow. Rizwan was the only batter who looked comfortable and kept accumulating runs with timely crucial boundaries. He counterattacked with Agha Salman and cruised to his fifty in quick time but couldn't convert it into a ton and fell against Cummins on 88. Salman Agha equally batted well with Rizwan and he stands unbeaten on 35 runs.

Ends with a dot does Mitchell Marsh and that will be Tea on Day 1! Fuller in length and just slipped down the leg side, Sajid Khan misses the flick and the ball dies on its way to the keeper. Pakistan are 198/6!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back after Lunch to start the second session on Day 1 of this third Test match between Pakistan and Australia. Australia is 2-0 up in the series and they have dominated the first session here in Sydney. The umpires and the players of Australia are back out in the middle and so are Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood who will resume their stay at the crease. The stage is set for an intriguing day of Test cricket, with the hosts asserting their dominance early on, and the visitors seeking resilience and revival. Join us for the next session, where the drama is poised to unfold, bringing with it the excitement and unpredictability that Test cricket is renowned for. Join us for the post-Lunch session at 7.40 am IST (2.10 am GMT).

With Shan Masood, the Pakistani captain, resiliently holding the fort on 32 and Mohammad Rizwan joining him at the crease, the duo aims to stitch together a partnership in an attempt to steady the ship for Pakistan. While the surface appears favorable for batting, the Australians have undeniably asserted their dominance in a session that unequivocally belongs to the hosts. The resilience of the Pakistani captain, coupled with the partnership-building efforts alongside Mohammad Rizwan, provides a glimmer of hope for the visitors. However, the Australians, sensing blood, will undoubtedly aim to capitalize on any lapse in concentration, setting the stage for an intense and action-packed second session.

As the first session of the opening day at Sydney draws to a close, the cricketing landscape resonates with the echoes of Australian dominance. After winning the toss and opting to bat, Pakistan finds itself at 75/4 after 24 overs, heading into the Lunch break. It has been an exemplary display of fast bowling by the Australian trio, as Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, and Josh Hazlewood opened their wicket accounts, leaving the Pakistani top order reeling. The Australian fast bowlers, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood made an immediate impact in their opening overs, each claiming a wicket to set the tone for a challenging day for the Pakistani batters. Starc's pace and Hazlewood's precision proved to be a lethal combination, pushing Pakistan on the back foot right from the start. The execution of their plans has been nothing short of clinical, consistently beating the bat and capitalizing on any hint of vulnerability displayed by the visiting batters. The skipper, Pat Cummins, led from the front, claiming two crucial wickets, including the prized scalp of Babar Azam, who was shaping up well until he fell victim to a sublime in-swinger.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the 3rd Test to begin! The national anthems are done and it is now time to get play underway and David Warner is greeted by all of his teammates as the Australian players take to the field. TOSS - Pakistan have won the toss and will BAT first.

Pakistan seemed lackluster in Perth but got progressively better in Melbourne with skipper Shan Masood leading the way with half-centuries in both innings and if they had been better in the field and done the small things better, they could have actually won the game but instead they are 2-0 down and have lost the series. Shaheen Afridi though has surprisingly been rested and that could also be a big talking point come the end of the game. Can the fight shown in Melbourne galvanize Pakistan and hand them crucial WTC points? Or will the Aussies ensure a whitewash in Warner's farewell Test match? We shall find out in due course. Toss and team news in a bit.

Australia haven't quite been at their best and faced a pretty stern challenge in the 'Boxing Day' Test and it required a special bowling effort from skipper Pat Cummins to ensure victory. But there were some solid performances from the likes of Steven Smith and Mitchell Marsh as well that contributed to the win. All eyes will once again be on David Warner as he gears up for his farewell Test match at his home ground and having announced a shocking retirement from ODI cricket too recently, 'The Bull' will look to make an impact and end on a high.

Hello and welcome to the Sydney Cricket Ground for our coverage of the 3rd and final Test match between Australia and Pakistan which will also be the 'Pink Test.' The hosts have already clinched the series but given the fight we saw from Pakistan in Melbourne, this one should be a proper game as there are vital WTC points up for grabs too.
